entities.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a sovereign nation in Southern Europe, Europe. Its capital is Sarajevo. Official languages include Bosnian, Croatian, Serbian. Government: Federal parliamentary constitutional republic (complex Dayton structure: two entities + Brčko District). Population: approximately 3.2 million. Area: 51,197 km². Comprehensive index for Bosnia and Herzegovina covering Illyrian/Roman heritage, medieval Bosnian kingdom (Ban Kulin, Tvrtko I), Bogomil heresy (Church of Bosnia), Ottoman conquest 1463 (~415 years, Islamization of part of population), Austro-Hungarian occupation 1878 (annexation 1908, Bosnian crisis), Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand (Sarajevo June 28, 1914, triggered WWI), Yugoslav kingdom, WWII Partisan resistance (Tito), Socialist Yugoslavia, Bosnian War 1992-95 (Srebrenica genocide, sieges, 100,000+ killed), Dayton Accords 1995, and complex post-war governance.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, triggered a chain reaction that led to World War I, one of the deadliest conflicts in human history, resulting in over 37 million casualties and reshaping the global landscape.
